title: RhymeSchemeLibrary
description: The rhyme patterns a lyric section can be written to. Patterns are letter strings over line positions: A, B, C are distinct rhyme sounds and X is a deliberately unrhymed line. Because the checker's rhyme detection is spelling-based and approximate, each scheme carries a strictness that says how much weight a mismatch deserves.

pattern.description: Letter string over line positions, e.g. 'AABB'. Parentheses mark a grouping, as in an internal-rhyme scheme.

strictness.description: strict = a mismatch is worth acting on; lenient = a mismatch is as likely to be the approximate detector's fault as the writer's.

kind.description: Which device the scheme governs. 'end' is checked against the end-rhyme pattern; 'internal' skips that comparison and instead requires interior rhyme pairs, because end-rhyme conformance is the wrong test for a verse carried by embedded rhyme; 'none' skips the rhyme check entirely.
